title: Lesson
description: One falsifiable rule written after a position closed. One JSON object per line in a .jsonl file. A lesson that is not falsifiable, or that would not have changed a decision, is an observation and does not belong in this file.

id.description: Stable id. Never reused, never renumbered after a merge.

cluster.description: Which lobe of the brain this belongs to. Clusters are free-form, but keep the set small — a brain with sixty clusters has no clusters.

rule.description: The lesson itself, stated so that it can be applied mechanically to a past position and produce a different decision. 'Be more careful' fails this field.

fingerprint.description: Stable hash of the normalised rule, used for deduplication. Two lessons with the same fingerprint MUST be merged rather than both stored. This is the field that stops a brain from holding the same lesson forty times.

weight.description: How strongly this lesson pulls on a decision. Grows with corroborating evidence, decays when a counterfactual contradicts it.

active.description: A retired lesson stays in the file. Deleting history is how you learn the same thing twice.

evidence.description: Closed positions this lesson was derived from or corroborated by. A lesson with no evidence is an opinion.

ref.description: Your own reference for the closed position. Deliberately opaque — this schema does not require you to publish your book.

outcome.description: confirmed: applying the rule would have improved the decision. contradicted: it would have made it worse. counterfactual_null: it would have changed nothing, which is why the lesson may not deserve to exist.

merged_from.description: Ids absorbed into this lesson. Populated by the merge step; its emptiness across a whole file is a symptom, not a clean bill of health.

supersedes.description: Lessons this one replaces outright, as opposed to absorbs.
